scope: AFS1-AFS8 only; later claims are not covered by this focused review
findings: AFS1: first maximum coefficient exists in the DVR norm; root division lowers its index and bounds distinct open-disk roots even in varying finite extensions. Multivariable evaluation and induction take place in actual finite extensions, without completing Qbar_ell or assuming an interior accumulation point.
AFS2: prime-to-ell residue roots and disjoint primitive ell-power levels give infinite Cartesian sets with precisely the index-distinctness condition; original ell=3 is included.

AFS3: the full actual KX3 local abelianization, including finite torsion and chosen free-coordinate lifts, makes torsion values on those lifts force finite inertia image; its open kernel descends through the same stored Artin quotient to one unit depth.

AFS4: the algebraic character extends from units with trivial chosen unramified factor; ASP2 supplies continuity for every algebra point. The original finPart is exactly the inverse of x(psi)*epsilon^i*delta.

AFS5: KX4-KX5 identify the supplied universal ring itself with the finite-variable power-series ring; the same Cartesian points are arithmetic with distinct finite parts and separate every element. The common-depth and admitted-weight clauses match source DenseWt/Good.
AFS6: the reversal h_i-i gives the original dominant weight and WtOf normalization; valuation/comaximal-prime and completion-density arguments make its global-embedding prescription consistent.
AFS7: both directions of local algebraicity use the actual Artin quotient, and CIP4 uniqueness preserves the every-IsLocalArtin quantifier.

AFS8: the coefficient point, epsilon^i sign, lowW+i formula, one common depth and injective indexing of finite parts agree literally with TWtBridge. The positive cyclotomic norm identity now explicitly cites CIP5; its dependency edge was added by the author.
corrections_resolved: Added explicit CIP5 citation and AFS8->CIP5 ancestry for the positive cyclotomic norm formula.

CIP1-CIP5 reciprocity including positive cyclotomic norm
